blocks.title: Secure Baselines and Hardening Targets comparison
Secure Baselines and Hardening Targets exam shortcuts
items: Need one approved configuration → ESTABLISH BASELINE
Define the secure standard before deployment.
Example: Document required password, logging, and service settings.
Need same settings on hundreds of systems → DEPLOY BASELINE
Use centralized configuration tools to apply the standard.
Example: Group Policy pushes workstation settings.
Example: Configuration management restores a disabled security control.
Unused switch ports create risk → HARDEN THE SWITCH
Disable unused ports and apply port security.
Example: Unused wall jacks map to disabled switch ports.
ICS cannot tolerate unplanned downtime → SAFETY + AVAILABILITY FIRST
Changes may need extra testing and maintenance windows.
Example: A controller patch is validated before production deployment.
IoT device still has factory credentials → CHANGE DEFAULTS
Example: Replace vendor default passwords before network connection.
blocks.example: Focus on what the resource needs: baseline consistency, hardening, secure access, isolation, authentication, or monitoring.

questions.q: A company first defines approved password, logging, and service settings for all Windows workstations. Which baseline step is this?
questions.explanation: Establishing a baseline means defining the secure standard.

questions.q: The approved workstation baseline is pushed to hundreds of computers through Group Policy. Which step is this?
questions.explanation: Deployment applies the baseline consistently across systems.

questions.q: A configuration-management tool detects that a required security setting was disabled and automatically restores it. Which step is this?
questions.explanation: Maintaining a baseline means detecting and correcting configuration drift.

questions.q: Unused access-switch ports are shut down and port security is enabled. Which hardening target is being addressed?
questions.explanation: Port security and unused-port shutdown are switch hardening techniques.

questions.q: A factory control system cannot tolerate unplanned downtime, so patches are tested carefully before deployment. Which target is this?
questions.explanation: ICS/SCADA hardening prioritizes safety and availability.

questions.q: A new network camera is placed into service with the vendor's default password still enabled. Which target is most directly at risk?
questions.explanation: IoT devices commonly have default-credential and patching risks.
